prs.title: Fix `token_expiry_time` upon context initialization for stored tokens.
prs.author: keurcien
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Tokens loaded from storage at OAuthClientProvider._initialize() never get token_expiry_time computed/restored, so is_token_valid() treats a stale stored access token as valid indefinitely. That skips the proactive refresh check in async_auth_flow, causing every access-token expiry after a process restart to fall through to a full interactive re-authorization instead of a silent refresh. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Tokens loaded from storage at OAuthClientProvider._initialize() never get token_expiry_time computed/restored, so is_token_valid() treats a stale stored access token as valid indefinitely. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: #1784 fixes the root cause directly in _initialize() (calls update_token_expiry on the loaded tokens) with a 4-line change plus an expired_tokens test fixture. #2875's own added code comment states the identical root cause ('a provider reloaded from storage never restores token_expiry_time, so is_token_valid() treats the stale token as valid') but works around it by inserting a new refresh-attempt step inside the 401/re-auth branch of async_auth_flow instead of correcting token_expiry_time itself — larger surface area in the request-handling hot path for a symptom that #1784 removes at the source.

prs.title: Fix substring matches in WWW-Authenticate parsing
prs.author: Whning0513
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both PRs fix the same bug in src/mcp/client/auth/utils.py: WWW-Authenticate header parsing used naive matching (e.g. substring/whole-header checks) instead of tokenizing into individual auth-params, so values could be matched incorrectly (partial/substring matches, or matches inside quoted strings/other params). Both add a comma-based tokenizer that tracks quote state and backslash-escapes to split the header into discrete auth-param tokens before extracting fields. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both PRs fix the same bug in src/mcp/client/auth/utils.py: WWW-Authenticate header parsing used naive matching (e.g. substring/whole-header checks) instead of tokenizing into individual auth-params, so values could be matched incorrectly (partial/substring matches, or matches inside quoted strings/other params). Both add a comma-based tokenizer that tracks quote state and backslash-escapes to split the header into discrete auth-param tokens before extracting fields. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: Both add an equivalent quote-aware, comma-splitting tokenizer (_iter_www_auth_params in #3012 vs _split_www_authenticate_segments in #3041) with the same escape/quote-tracking logic. #3041 goes further by adding _extract_bearer_auth_params, which splits on scheme boundaries within the segments (checking each segment's leading token against 'bearer') so it correctly isolates only the Bearer challenge's params when a header contains multiple challenges (e.g. 'Bearer ..., DPoP ...'). #3012's tokenizer only finds the first space in the whole header and treats everything after it as one flat param list, so it does not separate a second scheme's params from the first, making it incorrect for multi-challenge headers that #3041 handles.

clusters.pick_reason: Both add an equivalent quote-aware, comma-splitting tokenizer (_iter_www_auth_params in #3012 vs _split_www_authenticate_segments in #3041) with the same escape/quote-tracking logic. #3041 goes further by adding _extract_bearer_auth_params, which splits on scheme boundaries within the segments (checking each segment's leading token against 'bearer') so it correctly isolates only the Bearer challenge's params when a header contains multiple challenges (e.g. 'Bearer ..., DPoP ...'). #3012's tokenizer only finds the first space in the whole header and treats everything after it as one flat param list, so it does not separate a second scheme's params from the first, making it incorrect for multi-challenge headers that #3041 handles.

members.reason: [llm] duplicates #3041: Both PRs fix the same bug in src/mcp/client/auth/utils.py: WWW-Authenticate header parsing used naive matching (e.g. substring/whole-header checks) instead of tokenizing into individual auth-params, so values could be matched incorrectly (partial/substring matches, or matches inside quoted strings/other params). members.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both target the same trigger: the `attempt >= MAX_RECONNECTION_ATTEMPTS` exhaustion branch of `_handle_reconnection` in streamable_http.py, where a permanently-failed SSE reconnection previously left the caller with no resolution (the 'infinite reconnection loop' hang). members.cluster_pick_reason: #2395's diff shows a direct fix at the exhausted-retries branch: it builds a JSONRPCError keyed to the pending request's id (checking `isinstance(ctx.session_message.message, JSONRPCRequest)`) and sends it via `ctx.read_stream_writer`, which resolves the specific in-flight request that was awaiting a response — this is what actually breaks the hang described in the title. #3098 instead adds a `_unwrap_exception` helper that walks an exception/ExceptionGroup tree to pull out a `StreamableHTTPError`, implying its fix makes reconnection exhaustion raise and propagate as an exception through the task group rather than deliver an in-band JSON-RPC response to the waiting caller. Only #2395's visible diff shows code that unblocks the specific pending request id; #3098's visible diff only adds the unwrapping utility, with no shown call site tying it back to the pending request the way #2395 does.

members.author: Bartok9
members.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both patch the exact same conditional in validate_tool_use_result_messages() that fires when a tool_use block isn't followed by a tool_result — but they resolve it in opposite, mutually exclusive ways: #2962 makes the function skip validation entirely (no raise) when there are no tool_results, citing SEP-1577 as not requiring a tool_use to be followed by a tool_result; #3053 keeps the raise in that case but replaces the misleading 'ids do not match' message with an explicit 'tool_use blocks must be followed by matching tool_result blocks' error. clusters.pick_reason: Both add an equivalent quote-aware, comma-splitting tokenizer (_iter_www_auth_params in #3012 vs _split_www_authenticate_segments in #3041) with the same escape/quote-tracking logic. #3041 goes further by adding _extract_bearer_auth_params, which splits on scheme boundaries within the segments (checking each segment's leading token against 'bearer') so it correctly isolates only the Bearer challenge's params when a header contains multiple challenges (e.g. 'Bearer ..., DPoP ...'). #3012's tokenizer only finds the first space in the whole header and treats everything after it as one flat param list, so it does not separate a second scheme's params from the first, making it incorrect for multi-challenge headers that #3041 handles.

members.title: fix(auth): match complete WWW-Authenticate parameters
members.author: tarunag10
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #3041: Both PRs fix the same bug in src/mcp/client/auth/utils.py: WWW-Authenticate header parsing used naive matching (e.g. substring/whole-header checks) instead of tokenizing into individual auth-params, so values could be matched incorrectly (partial/substring matches, or matches inside quoted strings/other params). Both add a comma-based tokenizer that tracks quote state and backslash-escapes to split the header into discrete auth-param tokens before extracting fields.
